pr_title: settings: add a Sensitive option and use it for some settings
pr_body:
This new option causes the value of a string setting to be redacted in all outputs that are shown to the user. Users who have the MODIFYCLUSTERSETTING privilege can view the unredacted setting.

Virtual cluster setting overrides don't have their privilege checks changed for the write path. The only change is that when using SHOW commands, the values of sensitive settings will be redacted if the user does not have MODIFYCLUSTERSETTING.

See individual commits for details to make it easier to review.

fixes https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/115356

Release note (security update): Introduced the `server.redact_sensitive_settings.enabled` cluster
setting, which is false by default. If set to true, then the values of the following settings will be redacted
when accessed through SHOW commands or other introspection interfaces:
- server.oidc_authentication.client_id
- server.oidc_authentication.client_secret

In the future, any other sensitive cluster settings that are added will be redacted as well.
Users who have the MODIFYCLUSTERSETTING privilege can view the unredacted
settings.

Release note (cluster virtualization): If the `server.redact_sensitive_settings.enabled` cluster setting
is set to true, then the MANAGEVIRTUALCLUSTER privilege is required to view the values of the
per-virtual-cluster overrides for sensitive cluster settings.

Sure -- this PR doesn't change any of the existing checks for VIEWCLUSTERMETADATA. The only change is when displaying settings, whether it's a virtual cluster override or not, so that the two sensitive settings are only shown unredacted if you have the MODIFYCLUSTERSETTING privilege.

I think `ShowTenantClusterSetting` in sql/tenant_set is run _by a user in the system tenant_ to inspect the value of any overrides that are being applied to a secondary tenant. 

This code notably does _not_ check for `VIEWCLUSTERSETTINGS` today, but rather `VIEWCLUSTERMETADATA` (or `CanManageTenant` on the write path). 

I understand requiring a user -- including a user in a secondary tenant -- having `MODIFYCLUSTERSETTING ` in order to show the current value of a sensitive setting -- in their cluster, however it got there -- but I'm not seeing how that also suggests the user in the system tenant should need have `MODIFYCLUSTERSETTING` to see if an override is set, when they can _set_ the override without it (since that is off `CanManageTenant`).

I'll add that to the PR text as well as a `cluster virtualization` release note.

issue_context.title: sql: redact sensitive cluster settings by default
issue_context.body:
The following settings should not have their values revealed when using `SHOW CLUSTER SETTING`.

~Later on, we can add a privilege to view the unredacted value. For now, let's redact them unconditionally.~ See below; we will use `MODIFYCLUSTERSETTING`.

- server.oidc_authentication.client_id 
- server.oidc_authentication.client_secret

Epic: CRDB-33480

Jira issue: CRDB-33993
comments: synced with @dikshant - since we want to include this in 23.2, I'll mark this is a GA-blocker so we don't need to do a backport to a patch release later that is a backward-incompatible change.

Redact only these:
server.oidc_authentication.client_id
server.oidc_authentication.client_secret

After much internal discussion we don't think enterprise license is secretive enough to redact. And even then there are a bunch of places (eg DB Console) where it is exposed.

For now we can put them behind MODIFYCLUSTERSETTING. That way only the individual responsible for setting them is able to see them for troubleshooting etc.

Removing GA-blocker - since this is going to use MODIFYCLUSTERSETTING to determine if redaction is needed, we can introduce a new cluster setting that also can be used to opt-out of any redaction at all. This makes this change backportable.

@rafiss just wanted to check if you had a chance to consider this suggestion?

i had missed these comments since it wasn't marked as "changes requested." yes this idea sounds good to me. (though the `setting.InternalKey()`->`setting.Name()` and the usage of `decode_cluster_setting()` changes are both cleanups that i think we should keep.)
